beats.new_visual_element: One sentence, with and without its qualifier
beats.narration: The clearest case in Chapter 19 sent me back to the source text. It lists bleeding, bile leakage and a collapsed lung as risks of biopsy, in the case of hepatocellular carcinoma, a liver cancer. The chapter dropped those six words, so liver complications are now attached to biopsy of any tumour. Nothing was made up. A qualifier was lost.

beats.narration: One claim is simply backwards. Sensitivity is how many real cancers a test catches. Specificity is how rarely it raises a false alarm. The chapter says needle aspiration is high in sensitivity and variable in specificity. It is the other way round: when the needle finds cancer it is rarely wrong, but it can miss. One series I found reports specificity of 97 percent and sensitivity of 50.

beats.new_visual_element: Six errors fixed before I reached them
beats.narration: Chapter 27 surprised me. Six of its errors had already been fixed on the development branch by the time I reached them. One said the FDA gave a conditional approval, a category the FDA does not have. Another said no CRISPR therapy had passed phase two, when one is already approved. I could not just mark those as done. I opened each fix and checked it.

props.costLine: My job became checking the fixes.

beats.narration: The rest were still wrong. The chapter calls one virus the first cancer-killing virus approved. It was the first approved by the FDA. China approved one ten years earlier, and another source puts Latvia earlier still. Because the sources disagree on who was truly first, I limited the claim to the FDA rather than crown a different winner. Two more named the wrong viral vector for an eye therapy and the wrong clotting factor for haemophilia B.

beats.narration: These two chapters changed how I read a claim. I now look for what used to sit around it: a condition, a population, a date. And when someone has fixed an error before me, I check the fix instead of trusting it. Both chapters' corrections are now merged into the textbook.
